parsed.rationale: Emphysema on imaging has stronger and more consistent evidence for treatment-effect prediction. It was retained in all three penalized treatment-interaction analyses, had positive univariable R-learner validation gains in all three analyses, and showed positive causal-forest permutation R-loss increases in all three analyses, with causal-forest increases ranging from 0.002 to 0.004 and R-learner gains from 0.003 to 0.006. Its nominal interaction p-values were also fairly consistent, with two below 0.05 and one at 0.06, although multiplicity-adjusted q-values are unavailable. By contrast, serum creatinine was more clearly prognostic than predictive of treatment benefit: all three outcome models retained it, but validation R-loss gains were zero or negative in all three analyses, causal-forest permutation increases were only positive in one analysis, and penalized treatment interactions were positive in only one analysis. Creatinine did have two nominal interaction p-values below 0.05, but without adjustment for multiple testing and with weak validation-method support, this is less convincing. Uncertainty remains because the analyses use overlapping patient groups, effect sizes are small, and redundancy between the variables was not measured; nonetheless, the overall pattern favors Emphysema on imaging.
